name: OKRIN
author: completion-agent (sparse clue + forced completion)
description: Invented completion law over an ASCII letter grid. CLUE: k distinct capital letters, k in 3..5 (3-5 chars). Every character of the answer that is NOT one of the clue's letters is inert filler (the reference solve deliberately sprinkles non-clue capitals as decoys). Three things must hold. (1) SEED / forced completion: line 1 must begin with the clue string, so the answer extends a fixed seed the scorer rebuilds from the clue alone; no clue-independent witness can exist. (2) LOCAL, CHIRAL: for orthogonally adjacent letter cells, the RIGHT neighbour is the clue-cyclic successor and the cell BELOW is the clue-cyclic predecessor (so within one component the letter at (i,j) is clue[(j-i) mod k]); only local pairs are checked, so separate components may carry different offsets. No letter cell may be isolated - every letter needs at least one letter neighbour. (3) GLOBAL COUNT: a clue letter must occur exactly 2 + its ALPHABETICAL rank among the clue letters times (counts 2..k+1, keyed to alphabet order, NOT to clue order - the two clauses use two different orderings of the same letters, which is the second independent discovery). Totals: 9/14/20 cells. Intended discovery path: a demo shows only the clue's letters mattering and line 1 carrying the clue; counting letters gives 2,3,..,k+1 but in a scrambled order until the player tries alphabetical rank; tabulating adjacent pairs gives 'cyclically consecutive', which scores 0 forever until the player notices the direction (right=successor, down=predecessor). Witnesses closed: the clue alone and any single row fail the counts; a scatter of non-touching letters fails the isolation clause; a shifted rectangle or a full stripe grid fails the counts; an answer built for another clue is all-filler; a mirrored/rotated/indented answer fails the seed clause. Clues whose letters happen to be alphabetical (~5% of instances) score 1 under the wrong clue-order count hypothesis - a deliberate partial-credit gradient. Count profile base 2 was chosen because base 1 makes ~19% of rank permutations INFEASIBLE (support capacity: a class-t cell can only touch class t+-1 cells); with base 2 all k! profiles are comfortably satisfiable. generate is uniform over k in {3,4,4,5,5} and random distinct capitals. ITERATION 1 (measured, sim/results/lab-OKRIN-1, 2 Opus centaur players, 6x0.5s rounds, 5s cooldown, 1 demo/window, 3s final): MIXED - on target, rule left unchanged. OKRINa CRACKED in round 4 after 3 demos (0/610, 0/457, 10/597, 447/449, 444/445, 444/449; final 2685/2685 = 100%) and stated the rule correctly - right neighbour = successor, below = predecessor, alphabetical-rank counts, no isolated letter - plus two harmless extra beliefs ('the clue appears as a contiguous horizontal run', which my seed clause implies, and 'no fully enclosed blank cell', which the scorer does not check); it shipped one precomputed template per rank-permutation. OKRINb PARTIAL (final 2767/3804 = 73%): it found the alphabetical-rank counts and the Toeplitz law g[r][c]=clue[(c-r)%n] but never saw the seed clause as a rule, and instead learned a lookup table of accepted grid width mod n per rank-permutation from 226 labelled round-6 answers, so its accuracy tracked table coverage (n=3 100%, n=4 79%, n=5 53%). Both players confirm the intended discovery order; the seed clause is the last one found ('invisible until you are already at 99%'). Design property to preserve: three stacked clauses each score 0 alone, so a player with the count rule exactly right still scored 0/442 in round 5 - there is no partial-progress signal until every clause is right at once, which is what makes this hard. The decoy non-clue capitals in solve's output did their job (no template leak) but OKRINb reported them as a suspected bug and lost analysis time to them - intended, and documented here so an organiser can answer that question.
